title: Gemma, DeepMind's Family of Open Models — Omar Sanseviero, Google DeepMind

primary.label: AI Platforms & Developer Tooling
primary.rationale: The talk's primary object is the Gemma 4 model family itself, covering architecture (E2B, per-layer embeddings, MoE), training (140+ languages, Gemini tokenizer), and intrinsic capabilities (multimodal, multilingual). Gemma 4 is a general-purpose open model family with substantive coverage of healthcare applications (MedGemma, cancer therapy) and coding assistant use cases (on-device coding, Android Studio). The talk covers model pretraining and tokenizer design, LM Arena evaluation, and on-device deployment across phones, laptops, and edge devices. The talk balances accessible demonstrations with technical depth on the E2B architecture and per-layer embeddings, fitting an intermediate level. This is a conference presentation by Omar Sanseviero at the AI Engineer channel. All evidence anchors are graded as said_in_transcript, indicating direct statements from the talk.

summary: Omar Sanseviero introduces Gemma 4, Google DeepMind's newly released family of open models, emphasizing that open models can be downloaded, run on personal infrastructure, and fine-tuned for custom use cases. Gemma 4 ranges from 2B to 32B parameters. The smallest models run on Android phones, iPhones, and even Raspberry Pi, offering multimodal and agentic capabilities on-device. A MoE variant provides low latency, while the 31B model delivers maximum intelligence yet still fits a consumer GPU. A novel E2B architecture uses per-layer embeddings functioning as a lookup table, allowing only 2B parameters to load into GPU while the remainder resides on CPU or disk, optimizing for mobile. Gemma 4 adopts Apache 2 licensing, addressing prior community concerns. The models support multimodal understanding of images, video, and audio, including speech recognition and speech-to-translated-text. Trained on over 140 languages with a Gemini-based tokenizer, Gemma 4 enables fine-tuning for low-resource languages like Quechua. On-device demonstrations include an Android phone agent playing piano, on-device coding in airplane mode, and ten parallel Gemma instances generating SVGs at 100 tokens per second via llama.cpp. LM Arena scores position Gemma favorably in a small-but-capable quadrant. The ecosystem has reached 500 million downloads, 10 million for Gemma 4 base models in one week, over 1,000 Gemma 4 derivative models, and over 100,000 models total. Google collaborates with Unsloth, MLX, llama.cpp, Hugging Face, vLLM, and others. Android Studio integrates Gemma for offline agentic coding assistance. Official variants include Shield Gemma for content moderation and MedGemma for medical use cases including radiology and chest X-ray understanding. Community efforts include AI Singapore training models for Southeast Asian languages and Sarvam building national models for India's many official languages as part of sovereign AI initiatives. DeepMind researchers used Gemma 3 to propose cancer therapy pathways that were validated in an actual lab. Sanseviero encourages the audience to spend an hour experimenting with open models, noting that while API-based models offer the most raw intelligence, on-device open models now handle complex agentic tasks entirely locally with private data.

sections.title: Introduction to Gemma and Gemma 4 overview
sections.summary: Sanseviero introduces Gemma as Google DeepMind's family of open models that can be downloaded, run locally, and fine-tuned. He recaps Gemma 3 from a year ago (1B-27B, most capable open model fitting a single consumer GPU) and announces Gemma 4 (2B-32B), the most capable open models Google has released. Smallest models run on phones and Raspberry Pi; a MoE variant offers low latency; the 31B flagship fits a consumer GPU.

sections.title: On-device demonstrations
sections.summary: Live demonstrations show Gemma running fully on-device: an Android phone agent selecting skills like playing piano, on-device coding in airplane mode with no API calls, and ten parallel Gemma instances on a laptop generating SVGs at 100 tokens per second via llama.cpp. The speaker also mentions a community project running Gemma on a Nintendo Switch.

sections.title: LM Arena scores and Apache 2 license
sections.summary: LM Arena scores are shown with parameter count on the X-axis and score on Y-axis, positioning Gemma models in a favorable small-but-capable quadrant. Sanseviero notes models have improved over two years without growing larger. He announces Gemma 4's switch to Apache 2 licensing, addressing community concerns about the previous license.

sections.title: E2B architecture and per-layer embeddings
sections.summary: The E2B (effectively 2 billion) architecture is explained: the model has approximately 4B parameters but uses per-layer embeddings functioning as a lookup table rather than computation. Only 2B parameters load into GPU; the rest can reside on CPU or disk. This is optimized for mobile use cases and implemented via llama.cpp with a tensor override flag.

sections.title: Multimodal and multilingual capabilities
sections.summary: Smallest models handle multimodal understanding of images, video, and audio including speech recognition and speech-to-translated-text. The larger model handles fine-grained multimodal detail. Gemma 4 was trained on 140+ languages using a Gemini-based tokenizer, enabling fine-tuning for low-resource languages like Quechua. Multilingual and multimodal capabilities can be combined, e.g., explaining an image with Japanese text.

sections.title: Ecosystem growth and community adoption
sections.summary: Gemma 4 reached 10 million base model downloads in one week, with over 1,000 derivative models. The whole Gemma family has 500 million downloads and over 100,000 models. Google collaborates with Unsloth, MLX, llama.cpp, Hugging Face, vLLM, and others to ensure community-native tooling, emphasizing meeting developers where they already work.

sections.title: Product integrations and official Gemma variants
sections.summary: Android Studio features an offline agentic coding mode powered by llama.cpp or vLLM with Gemma, including Android-specific training data. The Gemmaverse has over 100,000 models total. Official variants include Shield Gemma for content moderation in production, and MedGemma (referred to as Med-Gemini in the talk) for medical use cases. Fine-tuning motivations are discussed including capability improvement, style changes, and domain-specific prediction.

sections.title: Community research, sovereign AI, and real-world applications
sections.summary: MedGemma is described as a multimodal Gemma 3-based model for medical tasks including radiology and chest X-ray understanding, and is open for further fine-tuning. Community efforts include AI Singapore training models for Southeast Asian languages and Sarvam building national models for India's official languages under a sovereign AI initiative. DeepMind researchers published a paper showing Gemma 3 proposing cancer therapy pathways that were validated in an actual lab. Sanseviero highlights diverse real-world use cases—finance, legal reviews, offline scenarios, Chrome extensions, and on-device control—and encourages the audience to spend one hour experimenting with open models, noting that while API-based models offer the most raw intelligence, on-device open models now handle complex agentic tasks with private data.
